title: Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint — Readout Template (Activation + Early Retention)
content:
PURPOSE
Use this doc as the standardized final readout format for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint. The goal is to make results legible across Growth, Product, Eng, Sales/CS, and Exec stakeholders, and to make decisions actionable (roll forward / iterate / rollback) with clear follow-ups.

Primary audience: Growth Marketing + Product + Eng + Sales/CS.
Secondary audience: Execs who want a concise “what changed / what did we learn / what are we doing next”.

How to use
- Keep the top section (TL;DR) to 1 page.
- Put raw tables, breakdowns, and screenshots in Appendices.
- Prefer “decision-ready” language: what we’re shipping, what we’re stopping, what we’re investigating.
- If data quality is compromised, explicitly state it and default to conservative conclusions.


========================
1) TL;DR (1 page)
========================
Sprint name:
- [Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint]  
Dates:
- Setup (Week 0): [YYYY-MM-DD → YYYY-MM-DD]
- Launch (Week 1): [YYYY-MM-DD → YYYY-MM-DD]
- Iteration (Week 2): [YYYY-MM-DD → YYYY-MM-DD]
- Readout (Week 3): [YYYY-MM-DD]
Owners:
- Growth sprint lead: [Ben Carter]
- Marketing ops / attribution: [Tyler Benson]
- Product (Console): [Marissa Cole]
- Eng (experimentation / instrumentation): [Jada Williams / Jin Woo Park]

What we changed (bullets)
- Emails: [e.g., 5-email onboarding series with triggers + suppressions]
- Console nudges: [e.g., setup checklist + 2 contextual banners]
- Retargeting: [e.g., LinkedIn/Google audiences for non-activated + lapsed]

Primary outcome (choose 1 primary metric; list others as secondary)
- Primary metric: [Activation within 72h: first_request_success] OR [Activation within 24h] OR [Time-to-first-success]
- Secondary: [D7 retention], [D14 retention], [billing_added], [created_deployment_or_route], [invite_teammate], [token_usage ≥ X]

Topline results (directional + magnitude)
- Activation within 24h: [Control X% → Variant Y%] = [Δ +Z pp], [p-value/CI if available]
- Activation within 72h: [Δ]
- Time-to-first-success (median): [Control A min → Variant B min] = [Δ]
- D7 retention: [Δ]
- Guardrails: [Unsub rate], [deliverability], [support tickets], [SLO/perf], [error rate]

Decision summary (explicit)
- Ship (roll forward): [Experiment IDs]
- Iterate (new variants): [Experiment IDs + what changes]
- Rollback / stop: [Experiment IDs + why]
- Data needs / instrumentation fixes: [List]

Key learnings (3–5 bullets)
- [Example: “Developers respond best to troubleshooting CTAs after an error event, not time-based reminders.”]
- [Example: “Checklist completion correlates with D7 retention, but incremental lift depends on surfacing streaming + cost dashboard steps.”]


========================================
2) Goals, hypotheses, and scope
========================================
2.1 Goals
- Increase activation (first successful production-like inference call).
- Improve early retention (repeat usage in week 1–2).
- Improve conversion into higher-intent milestones (billing added, token usage, routes/deployments, teammates).

2.2 Non-goals (keep us honest)
- [e.g., “Not optimizing long-term revenue this sprint.”]
- [e.g., “Not changing core API semantics.”]

2.3 Hypotheses tested (copy/paste from PRD; edit to reflect what actually shipped)
H1 (Emails):
- If we deliver a triggered onboarding sequence aligned to missing activation steps, then activation within 72h will increase and time-to-first-success will decrease, without harming unsub/deliverability.

H2 (Console nudges):
- If we provide an in-console checklist + contextual prompts for key steps (API key, first request, streaming, dashboards), then activation and D7 retention will increase, without increasing console latency or error rates.

H3 (Retargeting):
- If we retarget non-activated signups and recently lapsed users with developer-first proof points (latency/cost/reliability), then reactivation rate and return-to-product sessions will increase at acceptable CAC / CPA.

2.4 What shipped (actual scope)
- Emails:
  - [Email series name], cadence: [e.g., Day 0 / Day 1 / Day 3 / Day 7 / Day 10]
  - Triggering rules: [e.g., after signup, after api_key_created, after first_error]
  - Suppressions: [e.g., if activated; if unsubscribed; if sales-assist flagged]
  - Variants: [A/B subject lines, CTA variants]
- Console:

- Retargeting:

  - Audiences: [Non-activated within 7d], [Lapsed 14–60d]
  - Landing page: [Quickstart variant], UTM conventions: [link]
